items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: other artists like myself, — Jackie Wilson, The Drifters, The Clovers, The Flamingos, Chuck Willis, Roy Brown, Charles Brown, Wynonie Harris, to name only a few — was referred to as race music.

ctx.x: Could you talk about the music also being need-based?

Yeah, well the reason that what you say is very true is because at that time, when I first began recording, which was in 1948, the music that I sang or that other artists like myself, — Jackie Wilson, The Drifters, The Clovers, The Flamingos, Chuck Willis, Roy Brown, Charles Brown, Wynonie Harris, to name only a few — was referred to as race music. And it was not played by your top 100 stations. Basically, every southern town had a local radio station. The wattage wasn’t so powerful that you could hear what they…
Something I wanted to ask you is this. These records were not always nationally distributed either, where there was what they call Mom and Pop record stores.
